     9	# STP
    10	
    11	STP is a constraint solver (or SMT solver) aimed at solving constraints of bitvectors and arrays. These types of constraints can be generated by program analysis  tools, theorem provers, automated bug finders, cryptographic attack tools, intelligent fuzzers, model checkers, and by many other applications.
    12	
    13	* Homepage:      https://stp.github.io/
    14	* Ubuntu PPA:    https://launchpad.net/~simple-theorem-prover/+archive/ubuntu/ppa/+packages
    15	* Docker image:  `docker pull msoos/stp`
    16	
    17	
    18	## Build and install
    19	
    20	For a quick install:
    21	
    22	```
    23	sudo apt-get install cmake bison flex libboost-all-dev python perl minisat
    24	git clone https://github.com/stp/stp
    25	cd stp
    26	mkdir build
    27	cd build
    28	cmake ..
    29	make
    30	sudo make install
    31	```
    32	
    33	For more detailed instructions, see towards the end of the page.
    34	
    35	
    36	## Input format
    37	
    38	The file based input formats that STP reads are the: CVC, SMT-LIB1, and SMT-LIB2 formats. The SMT-LIB2 format is the recommended file format, because it is parsed by all modern bitvector solvers. Only quantifier-free bitvectors and arrays are implemented from the SMTLibv2 format.
    39	
    40	### Usage
    41	
    42	Run with an SMTLibv2 file:
    43	```
    44	stp myproblem.smt
    45	```
    46	
    47	Overflowing a 32b integer using the python interface:
    48	```
    49	import stp
    50	In [1]: import stp
    51	In [2]: a = stp.Solver()
    52	In [3]: x = a.bitvec('x')
    53	In [4]: y = a.bitvec('y')
    54	In [5]: a.add(x + y < 20)
    55	In [6]: a.add(x  > 10)
    56	In [7]: a.add(y  > 10)
    57	In [8]: a.check()
    58	Out[8]: True
    59	In [9]: a.model()
    60	Out[9]: {'x': 4294967287L, 'y': 11L}
    61	```
    62	
    63	With Docker:
    64	```
    65	docker pull msoos/stp
    66	echo "(set-logic QF_BV)
    67	(assert (= (bvsdiv (_ bv3 2) (_ bv2 2)) (_ bv0 2)))
    68	(check-sat)
    69	(exit)" | docker run --rm -i msoos/stp
    70	```
    71	
    72	## Architecture
    73	
    74	The system performs word-level preprocessing followed by translation to SAT which is then solved by a SAT solver. In particular, we introduce several new heuristics for the preprocessing step, including abstraction-refinement in the context of arrays, a new bitvector linear arithmetic equation solver, and some interesting simplifications. These heuristics help us achieve several magnitudes of order performance over other tools, and also over straight-forward translation to SAT. STP has been heavily tested on thousands of examples sourced from various real-world applications such as program analysis and bug-finding tools like EXE, and equivalence checking tools and theorem-provers.
    75	
    76	
    77	## Detailed Building and Installation
    78	
    79	STP is built with [CMake](https://cmake.org/), version 3.0.2 or newer. CMake is a
    80	meta build system that generates build files for other tools such as
    81	make(1), Visual Studio, Xcode, etc.
    82	
    83	### Configuration variables
    84	Here are a few interesting configuration variables. These apply to all
    85	generators.
    86	
    87	- ``CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE`` - The build type (e.g. Release)
    88	- ``CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`` - The prefix for install (e.g. /usr/local )
    89	- ``ENABLE_ASSERTIONS`` - If TRUE STP will be built with asserts.
    90	- ``ENABLE_TESTING`` - Enable running tests
    91	- ``ENABLE_PYTHON_INTERFACE`` - Enable building the Python interface
    92	- ``PYTHON_EXECUTABLE`` - Set python executable in case you have more than one python installed
    93	- ``SANITIZE`` - Use Clang's sanitization checks
    94	- ``STATICCOMPILE`` - Build static libraries and binaries instead of dynamic
    95	
    96	### Dependencies
    97	STP relies on : boost, flex, bison and minisat. You can install these by:
    98	
    99	```
   100	$ sudo apt-get install cmake bison flex libboost-all-dev python perl minisat
   101	```
   102	
   103	STP uses minisat as its SAT solver by default but it also supports other SAT solvers including CryptoMiniSat as an optional extra. If installed, it will be detected during the cmake and used:
   104	
   105	```
   106	$ git clone https://github.com/msoos/cryptominisat
   107	$ cd cryptominisat
   108	$ mkdir build && cd build
   109	$ cmake ..
   110	$ make
   111	$ sudo make install
   112	$ sudo ldconfig
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Building a static library and binary
   116	
   117	```
   118	$ mkdir build && cd build
   119	$ cmake -DSTATICCOMPILE=ON ..
   120	$ make
   121	$ sudo make install
   122	$ sudo ldconfig```
   123	```
   124	
   125	### Configuration and build options
   126	
   127	To tweak the build configuration:
   128	
   129	* Run ``cmake-gui /path/to/stp/source/root`` instead of ``cmake``. This
   130	  user interface lets you control the value of various configuration
   131	  variables and lets you pick the build system generator.
   132	
   133	* Run ``ccmake`` instead of ``cmake``. This provides an ncurses terminal
   134	  interface for changing configuration variables.
   135	
   136	* Pass ``-D<VARIABLE>=<VALUE>`` options to ``cmake`` (not very user friendly).
   137	  It is probably best if you **only** configure this way if you are writing
   138	  scripts.
   139	
   140	You can also tweak configuration later by running `make edit_cache` and edit any configuration variables, reconfigure and then regenerate the build system. After configuration, build by running `make`.
   141	
   142	You can use the `-j<n>` flag to significantly to decrease build time by running `<n>` jobs in parallel (e.g. `make -j4`).
   143	
   144	### Testing
   145	
   146	```
   147	git clone https://github.com/stp/stp
   148	git submodule update --init
   149	pip install lit
   150	mkdir build
   151	cd build
   152	cmake -DENABLE_TESTING=ON ..
   153	make
   154	make check
   155	```
   156	
   157	### Installing
   158	
   159	To install run `make install` and to uninstall run `make uninstall`. The root of installation is controlled by the `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` variable at configure time. You can change this by running `make edit_cache` and editing the value of `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`.
   160	
   161	
   162	### Building on Visual Studio
   163	
   164	Let's assume you put STP's source into c:\projects\stp and you have cygwin and
   165	git installed. Get zlib:
   166	
   167	```
   168	cd C:\projects
   169	git clone https://github.com/madler/zlib
   170	cd zlib
   171	git checkout v1.2.8
   172	mkdir build
   173	mkdir myinstall
   174	cd build
   175	cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="..\myinstall" ..
   176	cmake --build .
   177	cmake --build . --target install
   178	```
   179	
   180	Get minisat:
   181	
   182	```
   183	cd C:\projects
   184	git clone https://github.com/stp/minisat
   185	cd minisat
   186	mkdir build
   187	mkdir myinstall
   188	cd build
   189	cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="..\myinstall" -DZLIB_ROOT="..\..\zlib\myinstall" ..
   190	cmake --build .
   191	cmake --build . --target install
   192	```
   193	
   194	
   195	Get flex, bison, perl:
   196	
   197	```
   198	C:\cygwin64\setup-x86_64.exe  -qnNd -R C:/cygwin64 -s http://cygwin.mirror.constant.com -l C:/cygwin64/var/cache/setup --packages "flex,bison,perl"
   199	```
   200	
   201	Finally, Build STP:
   202	
   203	```
   204	cd C:\projects
   205	git clone https://github.com/stp/stp
   206	git submodule update --init --recursive
   207	mkdir build
   208	cd build
   209	cmake -DBoost_USE_STATIC_LIBS=ON -DENABLE_TESTING=ON -DPYTHON_EXECUTABLE="C:\Program Files\Python36\\python.exe" -DLIT_TOOL="C:\Program Files\Python36\Scripts\\lit.exe" -DMINISAT_LIBDIR="..\..\minisat\myinstall\lib" -DMINISAT_INCLUDE_DIRS="..\..\minisat\myinstall\include" -DZLIB_ROOT="..\..\zlib\myinstall" -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="C:\cygwin64" ..
   210	cmake --build .
   211	cmake --build . --target install
   212	```
   213	
   214	### Building Docker
   215	
   216	```
   217	git clone https://github.com/stp/stp
   218	cd stp
   219	docker build -t stp .
   220	echo "(set-logic QF_BV)
   221	(assert (= (bvsdiv (_ bv3 2) (_ bv2 2)) (_ bv0 2)))
   222	(check-sat)
   223	(exit)" | docker run --rm -i stp
   224	```
   225	
   226	
   227	# Authors
   228	
   229	* Vijay Ganesh
   230	* Trevor Hansen
   231	* Mate Soos
   232	* Dan Liew
   233	* Ryan Govostes
   234	* And many others...
   235
